subject: Maths
title: Proportion in context (recipes, maps, scale)
subtitle: Proportion · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can solve real-world proportion problems involving recipes, maps, scales, and exchange rates.

key_vocab.definition: scaling quantities up or down while keeping the same ratio between ingredients, distances, or values.
Recipes (scaling ingredients), maps (scale factors), currency exchange, and mixing ratios.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can solve real-world proportion problems involving recipes, maps, scales, and exchange rates.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content:
Proportion in context -- scaling quantities up or down while keeping the same ratio between ingredients, distances, or values.
Applications -- Recipes (scaling ingredients), maps (scale factors), currency exchange, and mixing ratios.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Find the scale factor (new ÷ original) and multiply all quantities by it.
Scale factor = &frac{new amount}{original}
Then multiply each ingredient/measurement by SF

Key examples:
  ✓ Scale 1:50000 means 1 cm = 50000 cm = 500 m  (map scale)
  ✓ Recipe for 4 → for 6: multiply by 1.5  (scale factor)
  ✓ £1 = .25 means £40 = 0  (exchange rate)
  ✗ Scale 1:50000 means 1 cm = 50 m  (forgot a zero: 500 m)
  ✗ Recipe for 4 to 6: add 2 to each amount  (must multiply by scale factor)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – scaling a recipe
  A recipe for 4 uses 200g flour, 100g sugar, 2 eggs. Make it for 6.
  Scale factor: 6 ÷ 4 = 1.5
  Flour: 200 × 1.5 = 300g, Sugar: 100 × 1.5 = 150g
  Eggs: 2 × 1.5 = 3
  300g flour, 150g sugar, 3 eggs
  (Multiply every ingredient by the same scale factor.)

Example 2 – map scale
  A map has scale 1:25000. Two towns are 8 cm apart on the map. Find the real distance in km.
  8 cm × 25000 = 200000 cm
  200000 cm = 2000 m
  2000 m = 2 km
  = 2 km
  (Convert from cm to km: divide by 100000.)

sections.title: Scaling recipes
sections.content:
Scale the recipe from 4 servings to the target.

(a) 200g flour for 4. Amount for 10?
(b) 150ml milk for 4. Amount for 6?
(c) 3 eggs for 4. Eggs for 12?
(d) 80g butter for 4. Amount for 3?

sections.title: Map scales
sections.content:
Calculate real distances from map measurements.

(a) Scale 1:50000. Map distance 6 cm. Real distance?
(b) Scale 1:25000. Map distance 12 cm. Real distance?
(c) Scale 1:100000. Real distance 8 km. Map distance?
(d) Scale 1:20000. Map distance 4.5 cm. Real distance?

sections.title: Currency exchange
sections.content:
Convert using the given exchange rate.

(a) £1 = .25. Convert £60 to dollars
(b) £1 = 1.15 euros. Convert £200 to euros
(c) £1 = .25. Convert 00 to pounds
(d) £1 = 1.15 euros. Convert 460 euros to pounds

sections.title: Mixing and ratios
sections.content:
Use proportion to solve.

(a) Concrete mix: 1 cement : 3 sand. Need 20 kg total. How much cement?
(b) Paint: 3 red : 2 white = pink. Need 2.5 L total. How much red?
(c) Squash: 1 part cordial to 4 parts water. Make 2 litres. Cordial needed?
(d) Model scale 1:72. Real plane 36 m. Model length?

sections.title: Mixed proportion in context
sections.content:
Solve each real-world problem.

(a) Recipe for 8: 600g pasta. Amount for 5?
(b) Map scale 1:40000. Towns 7.5 cm apart. Real distance?
(c) £1 = 145 yen. Convert £35 to yen
(d) A car uses 5 litres per 60 km. Fuel for 210 km?
(e) Scale model 1:200. Building height 4.5 cm. Real height?

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ Scale 1:25000 means 1 cm represents 250 m
✗ To scale a recipe from 4 to 6, add 2 to each ingredient
✓ To convert £ to euros, multiply by the exchange rate
✗ Scale 1:50000 means 1 cm = 50 m
✓ The scale factor for 4 servings to 6 is 1.5
